articleTitle: Induced Magnetic Anisotropy and Thickness Dependence of Magnetic Properties in Nanocrystalline Alloy "Finemet"
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetic field-induced magnetic anisotropy and thickness dependence of magnetic properties in the nanocrystalline alloy "Finemet" were investigated. Compared with amorphous alloys, it was difficult to induce a magnetic anisotropy in Finemet at low temperatures. However, magnetic anisotropy in Finemet could be easily induced by annealing at temperatures above 700 K, and the anisotropy increased with increasing annealing temperature and time. The magnetic properties of Finemet at high frequencies were improved by decreasing the thickness. This thickness dependence was similar to that for Co-based amorphous alloys. Thin Finemet materials are especially suited for use in magnetic components for use at high frequencies, because of their low core losses and high permeability at high frequencies.

articleTitle: Sputter Deposition of Ce-Substituted Iron Garnet Films with Giant Magneto-Optical Effect
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Epitaxial monocrystalline and polycrystalline films of highly Ce-substituted YIG have been prepared by rf-diode sputtering. The threshold temperature for epitaxial growth increased with Ce content at a rate of 80°C/CE ion from 390°C of YIG film. Epitaxy was achieved for Ce content up to 1.5 per formula unit. The Ce-substitution induced exceptionally large Faraday rotation in the visible and near infrared regions, the factor per Ce ion being 2 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> deg/cm at λ = 633nm and -1.3 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> deg/cm at 1150 nm. The polycrystalline films were obtained in single garnet phase for Ce content up to 0.7. They were fully crystallized when post-annealed above 775°C. The films were quite homogeneous and grain boundaries were indiscernible. Thus, Ce:YIG films are a very promising magneto-optical material.

articleTitle: Magnetic properties of Fe-Co-Ni films with high saturation magnetization prepared by evaporation and electrodeposition
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The Fe-Co-Ni based alloys have long been known as a soft magnetic material (perminvar alloy) which contains the features of high saturation magnetization exceeding 20 kGauss and a permanent permeability. However, there have been few reports on its wide composition range in relation to thin film materials. Fabrication possibilities have been confirmed over a wide composition range in regards to the Fe-Co-Ni based thin films based on the evaluation of the Fe-Co-Ni based thin film structure and magnetic properties with the sputtering evaporation method and alloy electrodeposition which employs the electrolytic plating method. Thus, in this report, we have focused on an examination of the relationship of the preparation method centering around composition adjustment with the film structure and magnetic properties. In regards to the high Bs compositions, the soft magnetic properties and corrosiveness of the electrodeposition films which have been formed in minute regions are examined and practical application to thin film head material has been examined.

articleTitle: Properties of Ultrafine Crystalline (Fe-Cu1-Nb3)-Si-B Quasi-Ternary Alloys and Improvement of Their Magnetic Properties by Magnetic Field Annealing
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The influence of the Si and B contents and of magnetic field annealing on the magnetic properties of ultrafine crystalline (Fe-Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-Nb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>)-Si-B quasi-ternary alloys were studied. An alloy containing 13.5 at% Si and 9 at% B exhibited the best soft magnetic properties. The relative permeability of this alloy at 1 kHz is about 1 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>. On the other hand, alloys containing about 2 at% Si and 13 at% B show a high flux density of about 1.55 T, and those containing about 17 at% Si and 5 at% B have nearly zero magnetostriction. Magnetic field annealing is very effective for improving the hysteresis curves of these alloys for many applications.

articleTitle: Influence of Yoke Construction on Magnetic Characteristics of Single Sheet Testers
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Iron losses measured by a single sheet tester depend on the construction of the yoke. The reason for this is examined through measurement and numerical analysis. The double yoke single sheet tester is recommended for use as a standard tester, because the eddy current distributions on the surfaces of the two sides of the specimen are different from each other when a single yoke tester is used.

articleTitle: Three Dimensional Magnetic Field Analysis of Permanent Magnet by Boundary Element Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Three dimensional analysis is necessary for complicated structural problems, but it requires substantial computer capacity. In this paper, the magnetic field of a permanent magnet was analyzed by the boundary element method. The calculated results were compared with measured results and were found to agree. This method reduces the computing capacity.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Stress and Magnetic Anisotropy Analyses for Thin Film Heads
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Stresses were calculated using the three-dimensional finite element method. There are two kinds of stresses, thermal and intrinsic. The latter were treated as equivalent thermal stresses and represented using modified thermal expansion coefficients. Modified values for films were selected so as to fit the calculated displacements to measured results, for circular substrates with a deposited layer. The accuracy of calculations was within 20% of measurements, and stress distributions near backgaps qualitatively corresponded to the domain structure observed by spin-polarized SEM. It was found that tensile stresses along the hard axis are dominant in the pole tip region. The dependence of the magnetic anisotropy on the magnetostriction constant was calculated using the stresses thus obtained. Suitable magnetostriction constants for the bottom yoke were found to be smaller than those for the top yoke.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of Accuracy of Rotational Magnetic Loss Measurement Apparatus
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetic field and loss in an apparatus for the determination of magnetic properties of electrical steel under rotational flux conditions using field sensing coils (H coils) is numerically analyzed by finite element calculations in order to improve accuracy. The method considered here is based on determination of field quantities and makes use of square-shaped samples and an airgap between the pole faces and the sample. Errors in field strength and loss are reduced by using optimum yoke construction and the double H-coil method.

articleTitle: High Magnetic Field Effect and Composition Dependence of Magnetooptical Kerr Rotation for the Heusler Compound PtMnSb
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetooptical Kerr rotation angle θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> for the polished surfaces of bulk PtMnSb samples was measured at 632.8 nm in strong magnetic fields. The saturation value of θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> for the stoichiometric sample was 1.42° in the as-polished state, and was improved to 1.75° by annealing at temperatures higher than 400°C. It is suggested that the improvement in θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> is caused by the decrease in the imaginary part of the diagonal elements of the dielectric constant tensor. It was also found that θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> depends strongly on the composition in the Pt-Mn-Sb ternary system, and takes a maximum at the stoichiometric composition.

articleTitle: Spin-Glass Behavior in Co-Ferrite Amorphous Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Amorphous Co-ferrite thin films not containing vitrifying elements were prepared by ion beam sputter deposition. Their magnetic properties were investigated by means of low-field dc magnetization and ac susceptibility measurements, which gave evidence of spin glass behavior. The temperature dependence of magnetization in a 50 Oe external field exhibited an irreversibility just below room temperature, which decreased with increasing field strength. A cusp in the ac susceptibility (80 Hz, 1 Oe) corresponding to the spin freezing temperature was observed at 284 K. Below this temperature, relaxation of the thermoremanent magnetization was observed. Besides this transition at 284 K, a sharp peak in the ac susceptibility at 86 K, suggestive of another transition, was observed. It is thought that spin glass ordering with a high freezing temperature is caused mainly by transition to an amorphous structure for strong superexchange interactions.

articleTitle: Stress Induced Magnetic Anisotropy of YBi2Fe5-xGaxO12 Sputtered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: In order to study the origin of perpendicular magnetic anisotropy in Bi-substituted iron garnet thin films, a series of samples with composition YBi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5-x</sub>Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> (0.36/≪x/≪0.97) was prepared by rf sputtering onto several substrates with various thermal expansion coefficients. The stress (σ) was calculated from the difference in thermal expansion of the film and substrate. The anisotropy constant (K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub>) of the films increased linearly with σ in the range from σ = -9.0×109 erg/cm3 to 3.0×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup> erg/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub> decreased linearly with x in the composition range studied. The experimental results are discussed and compared with results for Al-substituted films.

articleTitle: Reduction in Core Loss in Amorphous Cut Cores with Air Gaps
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: In order to reduce core losses in amorphous cut cores with air gaps, the effects of ferrite plates attached to the cut surfaces of the cores were investigated. It was learned that the attachment of thin ferrite plates decreases the core loss remarkably in such cores. It was also discovered that this method of reducing core loss is effective for magnetic induction levels up to 0.1 T. Computer simulation of the leakage flux in an amorphous cut core with air gaps suggests that this reduction is attributable to a decrease in the leakage flux perpendicular to the amorphous ribbon surfaces due to the attachment of the ferrite plates.

articleTitle: Magneto-Optical Observation of Magnetic Domains in Rubbing Surface of a Ferrite Head
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A magneto-optical microscope was used to observe in-plane magnetic domains. The magnetic contrast caused by the longitudinal Kerr rotation was optimized by adjusting an analyzer and a phase compensator. The contrast in the raw image detected by a CCD video camera was much improved by an image processor. Closure domains were clearly observed in both single layered and double layered permalloy thin square films. The magnetic domain wall was found to be Neel wall like. The observation revealed that the multidomain state is still stable in a 3 μm wide double layered permalloy film. Magnetic domains in rubbing surface of a ferrite head were successfully observed for the first. The magnetization reversal was expanded from near the head gap with reproducibility, when a coil current was increased in a direction opposite to the previous saturation current. A magnetization model was proposed to explain apparent hysteresis.

articleTitle: Permeability and Anisotropy Dispersion of Amorphous Soft Magnetic Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The frequency dependence of permeability has been calculated for soft magnetic thin films which have a uniaxial anisotropy with both amplitude and angular dispersion. These calculations have been performed for amorphous Co-Nb films, whose anisotropy dispersion has been determined by low-frequency FMR measurements. Comparison of the measured permeability with calculations suggests that the effective uniaxial anisotropy is dispersed more widely and with a smaller amplitude than is indicated by FMR measurements. The magnetization ripple is inferred to be one of the causes of the low value for the effective field.

articleTitle: Effect of Substrate Material on Growth of Bi-Fe-Oxide Films by Reactive Ion Beam Sputtering
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Non-thermoequilibrium Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf> garnet can be obtained by direct epitaxial growth onto a single-crystal garnet substrate from the vapor phase. Using a reactive ion beam sputtering technique and a target composed of 3Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and 5Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> (molar ratio), variations in the crystalline phase with the substrate material were investigated for a variety of substrates. The substrate materials employed were fused quartz, sintered alumina, and single crystals of MgO, SrTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, MgAl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> and Gd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> (ScGa)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>; films were prepared with these substrates at room temperature, at 480°C and at 540°C. The garnet phase did not appear on substrates other than single-crystal garnet. The thermoequilibrium phases BiFeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</inf> were formed only on alumina substrate. A new non-thermoequilibrium oxide with a Bi:Fe molar ratio of 3:5 was formed on the fused quartz, MgO, SrTi0<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and MgAl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> substrates by crystallization during deposition. The oxide was found to be antiferromagnetic at room temperature.

articleTitle: Magnetic Aftereffect Constant of Nd-Fe-B Sintered Magnets
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetic field and temperature dependencies of the magnetic aftereffect constant S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">v</inf> of Nd-Fe-B sintered magnets were studied for J-H demagnetizing curves between 293 and 400°K, the practical temperature range for permanent magnets. S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">v</inf> is constant and independent of the magnetic field in the range from the point near (BH)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> to the demagnetizing field whose magnetization J is -0.7 T. S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">v</inf> decreased linearly as the temperature was increased. The value of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">v</inf> and the temperature dependence of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">v</inf> for Nd-Fe-B sintered magnets were both considerably larger than for Sm<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</inf> sintered magnets.

articleTitle: The Stress-Magnetic Properties of Amorphous Magnetic Alloy
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Effects of internal shear stress applied by torque on the magnetic properties of Fe-based amorphous alloys were studied under weak magnetic fields of less than 800 A/m, where strips were helically bonded onto the shaft so as to form an angle of 45° with respect to the thrust direction. It was found that the permeability of each amorphous alloy in different gluing conditions reached for each sample a constant value above a certain torque and these torque values depend on the internal compressive strain applied by gluing A magnetization process model is considered to explain the above-mentioned behavior and states that the compressive stress affects the restraint of magnetic domain wall displacement.

articleTitle: Magnetic Moment and Curie Temperature in Amorphous Co-R Alloys
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetic properties of amorphous Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">100-x</sub>Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> (50 ≤ x ≤ 70) alloys prepared by a melt-quenching method were studied. Based on the results derived from the Co-Y alloys, the magnetic moment of Co and the Curie temperature in amorphous Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">100-x</sub>R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> (R = Pr, Nd, Sm, Gd, Dy, Er) alloys are discussed. The Co atoms no longer sustain a moment when x ≥ 60. The exchange integral between R and R atoms or between R and Co atoms rapidly decreases as the atomic number of the lanthanide element increases.

articleTitle: Formation of a Diffractional Grating by Magnetic Lithograph
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A new method to make an optical diffraction grating has been developed using the Bitter method. A periodic magnetic pattern like 0101 ... is written in a magnetic memory medium, and a magnetic fluid is used as magnetic toner to visualize this pattern. To enhance the contrast of the grating, an interfacial active agent in the magnetic fluid is destroyed by a certain organic solvent, and a DC magnetic bias field is applied to the memory medium to thicken the pattern. When a transparent grating is required, Au film is deposited on it as a parting agent after the formation of a magnetic toner pattern. After separation of the epoxy resin film from the memory medium, Au film is chemically etched. A sharp diffraction image is observed by projecting a laser diode onto the diffraction grating. Using this method, an optical grating can easily be made even on a convex or concave surface.

articleTitle: Development of the Absolute Type Magnetic Encoder Suitable for Thinner Structure
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Rotary encoders are often used as position detectors in robot control systems and are of two types: optical encoders and magnetic encoders. Magnetic rotary encoders have attracted attention for their durability in unclean environments, reliability at low temperatures, excellent shock resistance, and wide variety of designs. Such encoders can function in two different ways; detecting either relative or absolute positions. In this paper, an absolute position-detecting magnetic encoder with high resolution and a thin construction is proposed, and such an encoder (100 mm dia. × 20 mm) with 11 bits, only one-fourth as thick as conventional magnetic encoders, has been trial-fabricated.

articleTitle: Preparation and Soft-Magnetic Properties of Fe-Co-Ni-Cr Plated Films Having a Single Phase Structure and High Saturation Magnetization
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The authors investigated the method of preparation and soft magnetic properties of electrodeposited Fe-Co-Ni-Cr alloy film with high saturation magnetization and a single-phase structure. It was found that Fe-Co-Ni-Cr alloy film with a single-phase fcc structure can be electrodeposited at the cathode in a solution composed of Fe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>, Co<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>, Ni<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> and Cr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> ions and with SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2-</sup> as the count anion, by plating at current densities of more than 30 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Film consisting of Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">44</sub>Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">36</sub>Cr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> alloy, prepared by the plating method described in this paper, has soft magnetic properties (μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">iHA</sub> ≫ 1500, H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cHA</sub> ≪ 0.5 Oe, λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> = 6x10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>, B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> = 16,800 G) qualifying it for use in HDD thin film magnetic head cores.

articleTitle: Soft magnetic properties of Fe-Al-Si and Fe-Ni-Nb sputtered alloy films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The purpose of this experiment with the Fe-Si-Al thin film as an ordered structural alloy and the Fe-Ni-Nb thin film as a disordered structural alloy is to clarify the quantitative relationships and to improve the fabrication techniques in order to achieve improved soft magnetic properties. Thus, we examined in detail: 1) Concentration dependence of coercive force Hc and the effective permeability μeff. Furthermore, the relationship between μeff and the magnetocrystalline anisotropy and film magnetostriction. 2) The relationship between soft magnetic properties and the magnetic anisotropy field Hk, and the magnitude of long and short period local anisotropy fluctuation determined by the measurements of the dynamic differential susceptibility measurement. 3) The changes of μeff, Hk and long and short period local anisotropy fluctuation on a decrement of film thickness, in addition, the relationship between these amounts and K1 and λ.

articleTitle: Perpendicular Magnetic Anisotropy of TbFe, TbFeCo, and Dy-Fe Compositionally Modulated Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Compositionally modulated TbFe and TbFeCo amorphous films were prepared on glass substrates by the bias-modulated sputtering method. The modulated structure was confirmed for modulation lengths larger than 14 Å by X-ray small angle diffraction. Sharp layer boundaries were clearly observed using cross-sectional TEM. The magnetic perpendicular anisotropy energy K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub> increases with decreasing modulation length Λ, because of the interface anisotropy K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> which arises from the anisotropic ordering of Tb-Fe atom pairs or the internal stress at the layer boundaries. Dy-Fe multilayered films prepared by a vacuum evaporation technique were also investigated. As the periodic length Λ decreases, both the saturation magnetization M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> and the Kerr rotation angle θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> decrease sharply near Λ ≒ 40Å because of the change in the Fe crystal structure from bcc to fcc or amorphous. The perpendicular anisotropy k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub> increases proportionally to 1/Λ, with an interface anisotropy k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">S</sub> = 0.8 erg/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">S</sub> = 1.24 erg/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> at room temperature and at 80°K, respectively.

articleTitle: Magnetic and Magnetooptical Properties of Mn(Sb-Bi) Thin Films Fabricated by the Interdiffusion Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: NiAs-type Mn(SbBi) alloy films, with c-axes oriented perpendicular to the film surface, were obtained in the composition range 45 ≪ Mn ≪ 65 at%, Bi ≪ 10 at% by first forming an oriented SbBi layer by vapor deposition and annealing, then depositing an Mn layer onto this SbBi layer at an appropriate substrate temperature, and finally annealing at temperatures up to 500°C. Several different phases appeared in these films, the matrix of which was the NiAs type Mn (SbBi) phase. It was found that the phases and lattice constants of Mn(SbBi) change on increasing the annealing temperature. Systematic experiments on the magnetic anisotropy constant Ku and Kerr rotation angle θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> were carried out for the Mn(SbBi) films. As a result, substitution of Bi for Sb led to 1) an increasing K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub> value, and 2) a change in the wavelength dependence of θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub>. The maximum observed values of K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub> and θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> were 4.5 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> erg/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and 0.5° at H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ex</sub> = 7 kOe.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Sputtered Co-Ni/Cr Multilayer Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Multilayer films consisting of 70 at% Co-30 at% Ni alloy and Cr were prepared by dc magnetron sputtering. The number of (Co-Ni/Cr) bilayers and the ratio of the thicknesses of the Co-Ni and Cr layers were varied, while the total Co-Ni thickness was maintained at 900 Å. Appropriate combinations of the number of bilayers and the thickness ratio serve to improve both the coercive force and the squareness ratio of the films without an appreciable decrease in saturation magnetization. The change in saturation magnetization can be explained in terms of interdiffusion near Co-Ni/Cr interfaces. The change in the coercive force of multilayer films, the value of which is determined by the coercive force of the first Co-Ni/Cr bilayer, is controlled by the thickness of the Co-Ni layers.

articleTitle: Characteristics of Parametric Reproducing Head for Perpendicular Magnetic Recording
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A magnetic reproducing head using parametric oscillation has been developed for use in perpendicular magnetic recording. The head is based on parametric oscillation in a resonant circuit consisting of a single pole-type perpendicular magnetic recording head and four varactor diodes for time-variable capacitance. In this paper, the principle of data reproduction as well as experimental results are described. The characteristics of the output voltage are independent of the signal frequency in the range from DC to 3 MHz. The output voltage is proportional to input signals up to 1 V.

articleTitle: Film Composition and Perpendicular Magnetic Anisotropy of Electroless-Plated CoNiReP Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetic properties and microstructure of electroless-plated CoNiReP films, which varied primarily in their cobalt content, were investigated in order to clarify the origin of their magnetic anisotropy. The films which showed perpendicular magnetic anisotropy contained approx. 25 to 40% cobalt. They also had a higher crystallinity and better c-axis orientation than does hep cobalt. It is thought that the anisotropy of these films is mainly due to the crystalline anisotropy deriving from the micro structure, and that the smaller M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">S</inf> values, which act to decrease the demagnetizing field, enhance the anisotropy. The shape anisotropy caused by segregation in films is also thought to affect the overall anisotropy.

articleTitle: Magnetic Field Modulation Recording on GdDyFeCo Magnetooptical Disk
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The characteristics of magnetic field modulation recording on GdDyFeCo magnetooptical disks were investigated. The GdDyFeCo recording layer was deposited by a two-source RF magnetron sputtering method. The thermomagnetic properties of the compositionally modulated films varied with the modulation periodicity, and the recording field (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>) was smallest at a modulation period of 2 Å. On determining the dependence of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> on the GdDy content, a relatively low H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> was found to appear in the rare earth-rich region near the compensation composition. By optimizing the GdDy content, recording magnetic field transition times of less than 250 ns can be obtained at a recording frequency of 720 kHz.

articleTitle: Magnetic Recording Properties of Spinel Rich Barium Ferrite Tapes
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Perpendicularly and longitudinally oriented (PO and LO) tapes were prepared from spinel-rich barium ferrite pigments with different coercivities H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>. The SFD and SFDr for LO tapes were much smaller than for metal particulate (MP) tape. Tape outputs were measured on a drum tester using a Sendust sputtered sheet laminated head. In the low recording density region, the LO tapes yielded higher output than the PO tapes, but at high recording densities, the PO tape output was about 3 dB higher than for LO tapes with nearly the same H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> in the oriented direction. The D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</inf> of the LO tape was greater than that of MP tape with almost the same longitudinal H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>.

articleTitle: Frequency and Field-Intensity Dependences of Permeability of Soft Magnetic Films and their Expression Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The permeabilities of soft magnetic films (sputtered CoNbTaZr) were measured under a wide range of field amplitudes (8 mOe to 8.5 Oe) at high frequencies (10 kHz to 1 MHz). In order to express the frequency (f) dependence of the permeability simultaneously with the field-intensity (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ex</inf>) dependence, a method for expressing the permeability characteristics was proposed employing constant-permeability contour lines in the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ex</inf>-f plane. It was found that such contour patterns reflect the process of magnetization of soft magnetic films in different areas of the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ex</inf>-f plane. The behavior of the contour lines for films with uniaxial magnetic anisotropy was investigated in particular. The permeabilities and magnetization processes are different for different manners of magnetic excitation, even at the same values of f and H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ex</inf>. The difference may be attributed to the irreversible movement of magnetic domain walls.

articleTitle: Magnetic and Magnetoresistive Properties of Au/Co Superlattices
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Au/Co artificial superstructure films were prepared by an alternating deposition technique in ultra-high vacuum. A large perpendicular anisotropy was found to occur when the Co layers were thinner than 20 Å. From torque measurements the maximum value of K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⊥</sub> at room temperature was estimated to be 9.6 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> erg/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The surface anisotropy energy constant K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> was about 0.4 erg/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The magnetoresistivity was measured as a function of a perpendicular applied magnetic field. The magnetoresistivity curve obtained was hysteretic, showing a peak in the vicinity of H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>. The maximum change in resistivity was about 4% at 77 K.

articleTitle: Surface Morphology of the Grain of Permalloy Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Surface morphologies of sputtered permalloy films were investigated by SEM. Grain sizes decreased with slanting of the substrate surface or the presence of N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> in the sputtering gas. The preferred orientations of permalloy films were changed from ≪111≫ to ≪100≫ by the N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> presence. SEM observations of crystal orientations suggested that the changes in the preferred orientations of permalloy films were caused by reduction of the surface energy, which was, in turn, thought to be caused by nitrogen adsorption.

articleTitle: Non-contact Stress Measurement of Rail Steel Using a Magnetic Anisotropy Sensor
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The Magnetic Anisotropy Sensors (MAS) is based on the fact that when stress is applied, the magnetic anisotropy of steel materials changes. MAS employs a small, light probe and is capable of non-contact stress measurement. This paper describes experimental results for non-contact stress measurements of rail steel. A specimen was cut from an actual 60 kg steel rail, and tensile and compressive stresses were applied using a fatigue testing machine. Good linearity of the MAS output voltage to the applied stress was observed over tensile stresses between 0 and 160 MPa when demagnetization was employed.

articleTitle: Non-Destructive Detection of Drop Out by a Measurement Tape/Head Contact Condition
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: With the recent increases in recording density of VCRs, tape/head interface problems have become much more immediate. Magnetic recording characteristics such as dropout are greatly affected by dust and by microscopic irregularities or protrusions on the tape surface. In this paper, we report on the non-destructive detection of dropout using a system which measures the state of tape/head contact. Experiments have shown that stretching of the tape/head spacing was several hundred times the height of protrusions, and that the coefficient of the record/playback spacing loss was 100 dB.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties and Kerr Effects in PtMnSb Thin Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Dependence of magnetic properties and Kerr effects in PtMnSb thin films on oxygen partial pressure during annealing was investigated. The coercivity H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c⊥</sub> increased with oxygen partial pressure, while the change in H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c″</sub> was relatively small. The saturation magnetization M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> was almost constant up to 6 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> Torr, and then decreased rapidly at higher O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> pressures. The Kerr rotation angle in zero magnetic field θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K(0)</sub> and the squareness ratio R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> of Kerr loops took on maximum values at or near 8 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> Torr of 0.85° and 0.45 respectively. SEM observations and X-ray diffraction studies revealed that these values are related to the preferential oxidation at PtMnSb columnar boundaries. The oxidation may shorten the size of columns and isolate them from each other.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties and Magnetoresistance Effect in Evaporated NiFeCo Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The anisotropic magneto-resistance (MR) ratio and magnetic anisotropy field H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> have been examined for (Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.82</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.18</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">100-x</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> and Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">82</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18-x</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> evaporated films, both as-prepared and after annealing at 320°C for two hours, to evaluate their usefulness as MR head materials. The MR ratio of the (Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.82</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.18</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">100-x</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> is almost constant regardless of changes in the Co concentration. The MR ratio for the Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">82</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18-x</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> films increases as the Co concentration increases, and after annealing the MR ratio rises up to 5% in the range of Co concentrations above 6 at%. The H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> increases as the Co concentration is increased, and is not changed by annealing. The increase in the MR ratio for Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">82</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18-x</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> films due to annealing is related to inhomogeneous strain and lattice defects. For Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">82</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> film, an MR ratio of 5.1% and an H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> of 7.0 Oe were obtained, making such film suitable for application in MR heads.

articleTitle: Properties and structure of AlSiN and AlSiON films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Magneto-optical disks employ rare earth-transition metal amorphous alloy films (RE-TM films) as recording films, therefore improvement of the corrosion resistance of such disks is an important problem which must be resolved to enable practical application. Development of protective layers for magneto-optical disks is important to improving corrosion resistance. Such protective layers must offer excellent protective performance, and must also have a large refractive index in order that a large Kerr effect enhancement be obtained. AlSiN and AlSiON films are being developed for use as protective films meeting these requirements. However, as yet not much is known about the structure, bonding states, and relation between composition and refractive index of such films. This article reports on the refractive indices, structures, and bonding states of AlSiN and AlSiON sputtered films.

articleTitle: Effect of Excitation Magnetic Field on Characteristics of Magnetostrictive Torque Sensors
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Characteristics of a magnetostrictive torque sensor were studied in the excitation current range 10~1000 mA and at excitation frequencies from 1 kHz to 100 kHz. Ni-Cr-Mo steel (JIS standard SNCM439) ferromagnetic material was used in an experimental shaft because of its high mechanical strength under applied torques ranging - 1500~1500 Nm. As the excitation current was increased, the sensor sensitivity was markedly enhanced and the hysteresis and offset deviation along the shaft circumference were reduced. Good sensor output has been obtained at large excitation currents exceeding 200 mA. In addition, a new memory phenomenon, which seems to consist of changes in magnetic domains induced by torque-generated stresses, has been discovered in the small excitation current range.

articleTitle: Magnetic Anisotropy and Columnar Structure of Fe Films Made by Simultaneous Evaporation with Oblique Incidence from Two Sources
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Fe film samples were prepared by oblique simultaneous evaporation from two sources with an angle Ø between the two planes of incidence, the magnetic anisotropy in the film plane was measured, and the columnar structure was observed by SEM. For samples prepared with Ø≤45°, the easy axis of anisotropy and columnar grain alignment are in the direction perpendicular to the plane bisecting the two planes of incidence; for samples with Ø≥45°, they are parallel to the bisecting plane. A mechanism of anisotropic arrangement of the columnar grains based on a self-shadowing effect is proposed. The magnetic anisotropy calculated from the columnar structure assuming such a mechanism was in fairly good agreement with the measured anisotropy.

articleTitle: Relationship between Head/Tape Contact Conditions and Tape Stiffness
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: An experimental study on the tribology of head/tape interfaces has been carried out in order to develop high-performance videotapes. In this paper, we report on a system for directly measuring the head contact force, and describe the relationship between contact conditions and tape stiffness. The video head was found to exert a contact force of about 20 to 30 mN, and the steady-state distribution of this force over all angles of rotation of the cylinder is approximately expressed by an exponential function. Under low stiffness conditions, the distribution becomes less well-ordered, and the playback signal deteriorates. It is thus very important that a suitable stiffness be maintained, to obtain a stable state of head/tape contact.

articleTitle: Inductance and Read-Write Characteristics for Thin Film Heads
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The inductance and read-write characteristics for thin film heads with various magnetostriction constants were investigated. Heads consisting of a top yoke with positive magnetostriction constants and a bottom yoke with negative constants, exhibited excellent read-write characteristics. Such a result can be explained by an increase in the difference between the inductance at zero bias, and that when the core pieces are magnetized, that is, by the permeability of the core pieces. High permeability was caused by the magnetoelastic effect based on the induced uniaxial stresses in permalloy films. In addition, the overwrite level improved dramatically as certain values of the bias magnetomotive force, determined from the inductance characteristics, increased. It was concluded that the measurement of the inductance characteristics is a very powerful method for evaluating the performance of pole tips and taped regions of thin film heads.

articleTitle: Magnetostriction Measurements for Amorphous Wires
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Measurements of the saturation magnetostriction constant λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> of amorphous wires have been difficult using conventional techniques, due to their very small diameters (10~125 μm). This paper describes the stable measurement of the magnetostriction of amorphous wires, using a magnetization rotation model and applying a compressive stress to positive-magnetostriction wires and a tensile stress to negative-magnetostriction wires. A value for λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">S</sub> of 35 ppm was obtained for an as-prepared Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">77.5</sub>Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7.5</sub>B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</sub> wire at room temperature.

articleTitle: High Frequency Permeability of Thin Film Magnetic Core
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetization process of a thin film magnetic core at high frequencies was studied, using a simple magnetic closed circuit with a 17-turn coil. The permeabilities μ, μ' and μ" were measured. Below 5 MHz, μ and μ" increased with the coil current; this increase was inferred to be due to domain wall movement. Above 5 MHz, μ did not increase with the coil current, and it is assumed that domain wall movement does not occur readily above 5 MHz. The magnetic flux density in the core was calculated for frequencies 0.1 MHz~20 MHz, and was found to decrease with the frequency. Because domain walls do not move easily at high frequencies, it is expected that the flux in triangular domains at the edges of the core decreases with increasing frequency.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Perpendicular Anisotropy of Magnetooptical Recording Film Using 45° Hall Effect Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The author has developed a new method to measure the effective magnetic anisotropy field H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>' of RE-TM magnetooptical recording film using the spontaneous Hall effect. By this method, the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>' can be obtained from measurement of the spontaneous Hall loop with respect to a magnetic field applied obliquely, at 45° from the normal to the film. The value of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>' obtained by the Hall method agrees fairly well with values determined by the conventional VSM/torque method. This paper describes the new method and presents experimental results.

articleTitle: Recording Characteristics of MR Head for Hard Disk Drive
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A disk drive head combining a shunt-biased MR read element and a multi-turn inductive write element, designed for use in 2.5" hard disk drives, was studied in these experiments. The MR element, consisting of an Ni-Fe film, is positioned in the inductive write gap. The write core consists of Mn-Zn ferrite and Co-Zr-Nb-Ta amorphous film, and has a "shaped-rail" air-bearing surface to achieve high reliability at low flying heights, such as 0.15 μm. Outputs of 0.54 m<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p-p</sub> in longitudinal recording, and 0.35 m<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p-p</sub> in perpendicular recording, were obtained from the MR-inductive combination head at a medium velocity of 4.7 m/s, a flying height of 0.15 μm, and a track width of 10.0 μm. Moreover, in spite of the fact that the MR element did not have a center tap, second harmonic distortions were decreased to less than μ26 dB.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Fe/Al Multilayered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The structures and magnetic properties of Fe/Al multilayer thin films prepared by dc magnetron sputtering have been investigated. The crystal structure and magnetic properties of films were found to depend on the thickness ratio of the Fe and Al layers (dFe/dAl). The lattice constant increases with decreasing thickness ratio, because solid solutions of Fe and Al are formed in the interface layers. For thickness ratios below 3, the lattice constant increases discontinuously and the saturation magnetization of the iron layer decreases rapidly with decreasing thickness ratio. In this region, ordered structures such as Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Al seem to be formed, resulting in a decrease in H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> and an increase in the resistivity with decreasing thickness ratio. Films with layer thicknesses dFe = 18 Å and dAl = 6 Å had H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> = 1 Oe and M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> = 1200 emu/cc.

articleTitle: Structure and Magnetic Properties of Sendust/Under-Layer Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Sendust MIG (metal-in-gap) heads have been developed for use in high density recording systems. Al oxidization at the boundary between the Sendust film and the MnZn-ferrite, however, acts to degrade the soft magnetic properties, and insertion of Ni-Fe film between them is an effective way to rectify the problem. In the present paper, the effects of Ni-Fe film insertion are investigated in detail, with the following results: 1) X-ray diffraction intensity from the (110) plane is stronger for Sendust film on Ni-Fe/MnZn-ferrite than for MnZn-ferrite. 2) Ni atoms in the Ni-Fe film diffuse into the Sendust film with annealing at 550°C and over. 3) Little degradation of the permeability and coercivity is observed for Sendust film containing less than 1.4-wt% Ni.

articleTitle: Magnetic and Magneto-Optical Properties of MnAI Alloyed Film
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: MnAl films, prepared with an Mn/Al multilayer structure by vacuum evaporation, were studied. In the Mn content range of 31 to 40 at%, films became ferromagnetic (τ phase) on annealing at from 220 to 420°C. They show the same X-ray diffraction lines of the fct (Cu-Au I) structure as do bulk MnAl alloys, although the range of Mn contents resulting in the τ phase is quite different, at 51 to 59 at%, from that for the bulk material. In these films, the τ phase is intermixed with a nonmagnetic η phase below 34 at% Mn, and with a ß phase above 36 at% Mn. The M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> changes with the Mn content, and shows a maximum of approximately 330 emu/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> at about 36 at% Mn. The coercivity H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> increases from 1 to 6 kOe with increasing Mn content. The Kerr angle θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> increases with decreasing wavelength λ, reaching a value of about 0.17° at 400 nm, while the reflectivity R has a value of above 40% in the visible wavelength range.

articleTitle: Magnetostriction of Amorphous Pr0.2(Fe1-xCox)0.8 Alloys
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetostriction of amorphous Pr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</sub>(Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.8</sub> alloys (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.6) and Pr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</sub>(Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.8</sub>Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</sub>) × (Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.43</sub>B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.57</sub>) × (0.7 ≤ x ≤ 0.85, 0.15 ≤ y ≤ 0.3, 0 ≤ z ≤ 0.3) alloys was measured in the temperature range from 77 to 400°K. The value of the magnetostriction λ (λ=(2/3) [Δ1/1)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">″</sub>-(Δl/l)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⊥</sub>]) for Pr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</sub>(Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.8</sub> exhibits a maximum at x=0.2; it is about 760 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> at 77°K and 260 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> at room temperature. The temperature dependence of the magnetostriction is discussed in terms of the single-ion model.

articleTitle: Magneto-Optical Spectra in Single Crystals of Cr-Te Compounds
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Optical and magneto-optical properties of single crystals of Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Te<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Te<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>, grown by the chemical vapor transport technique, were studied. The reflectivity spectra at normal incidence of both samples were measured at room temperature, and the magneto-optical spectra of the Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Te<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> were also measured. Spectra of the diagonal and off-diagonal elements of the conductivity tensor were obtained from the measured spectra. These were compared with estimations based on density of state curves calculated by Dijkstra, and showed reasonably good agreement. From these results it is concluded that transitions from Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3d</inf> to the Conduction Band for majority spins and Te<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5p</inf> to Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3d</inf> for minority spins, are responsible for the observed optical absorption and magneto-optical effects.

articleTitle: A New Measurement System of the Surface Magneto-Optic Kerr Effect (SMOKE)
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A new system for measuring the surface magneto-optical Kerr effect (SMOKE) has been developed. The combination of a polarization modulating method using electrical detection, and signal processing using a computer, provides a very high sensitivity of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> degrees and a good signal-to-noise ratio. Moreover, electrical calibration using a Faraday cell makes it possible to measure the absolute value of a Kerr rotation angle of order 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> degrees. The SMOKE hysteresis of a two-atomic-plane layer of fcc-Co grown on a Cu (100) surface was successfully measured; its Kerr rotation angle is about 5×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> degrees.

articleTitle: Magnetic and Magneto-Optical Properties of Pd/Co Multilayered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetic and magneto-optical properties of Pd/Co multilayered films prepared by rf sputtering have been investigated. The perpendicular magnetic anisotropy of films increases as the layering period λ and Co content are decreased. The maximum value obtained for the anisotropy K⊥ was 3.8 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> erg/cc, where λ and the Co content were 11 Å and 28 at% respectively. The saturation magnetization increases as λ decreases, approaching the same value as for the alloys. The Kerr spectra of multilayered films and of alloy films are alike in having a peak near the wavelength of 400 nm, and they are almost the same when λ ≪ 15 A. These results suggest that the perpendicular anisotropy results from compositionally modulated structures with interfacial alloying rather than wdth sharp bilayer interfaces.

articleTitle: Development of a Permanent Magnet Assembly for MRI
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A permanent magnet assembly for MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) has been developed using a high-energy product sintered Nd-Fe-B magnet. There are three types of magnet assembly for use in MRI: superconductive electromagnets, conductive electromagnets, and permanent magnets. The last does not require liquid helium, electricity or cooling water, and can be installed in small spaces. Despite these advantages, however, permanent magnet assemblies have not been widely adopted, mainly because of the difficulty of attaining uniformity on the order of ppm, and the tremendous weight of such magnets. However, a high-energy product Nd-Fe-B magnet developed in 1983 has made it possible to realize MRI based on permanent magnets. Using such a magnet and investigating the optimum configuration of pole pieces with shims, we obtained a Pk/Pk deviation of 30 ppm over a 35 cm diameter spherical volume at the center of the air gap.

articleTitle: On the Enhancement of the Magneto-Optical Kerr Rotation for PtMnSb by Annealing
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magneto-optical Kerr rotation angle θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> for polished bulk PtMnSb was found to be greatly enhanced after annealing at temperatures above 400°C, although the change in the spectrum of the reflectance R was very small. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy analysis, and calculation of R and θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> assuming the formation of an overlayer, indicated that the enhancement of θ<subf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K is not attributable to an overlayer effect. It was found that the enhancement of θ<sub>K</sub> was instead correlated with the change in magnetic anisotropy at the surface due to annealing.</subf>

articleTitle: Pseudo Output and Magnetic Properties of Fe-Al-Si Film in MIG Head
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: In Fe-Al-Si film deposited on ferrite material, there is a layer near the film-ferrite interface with inferior magnetic properties. This layer, which acts as a pseudo-gap in MIG heads, is caused by the nonuniform structure of the Fe-Al-Si film and by interdiffusion between film and ferrite. Improvement of the properties of these Fe-Al-Si films requires better crystal orientation, smaller grain sizes and a homogeneous film structure; these changes can be attained by selecting the optimum substrate. When a MIG head uses the (110) face of single-crystal ferrite as a gap surface, the head exhibits no pseudo-output, nor does a MIG head of polycrystalline ferrite with a Fe-Al-Si/Fe-Ni double-layer film, because both MIG heads have good crystal orientation and a homogeneous film structure.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Rapidly Quenched (Fe1-xCox)17Sm2 Alloys
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The formation and magnetic properties of metastable TbCu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>-type disordered compounds in rapidly quenched (Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub>Sm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> (0 ⩽ x ⩽ 1.0) alloys were investigated by X-ray diffraction and thermo-magnetic analysis. The disordered compound was formed in a single phase in the range 0.5 ⩽ x ⩽ 1.0 at a disk speed of 42 m/s. The disordered phase is magnetically harder than the ordered phase with a Th<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Zn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sub> structure.

articleTitle: Influence of Wiggle on Reproduced Waveform
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: In the reproduced waveforms from thin film magnetic heads, distortions ("wiggles") are occasionally observed. In this study, a method for extracting wiggles from the reproduced waveform was devised, and the characteristics of wiggles were studied. The extracted wiggles had a pulse width of from 40 to 80 ns, and an amplitude of from 10 to 30 μV Their positions in the reproduced waveform were shifted by an external magnetic field, but the wiggle width and amplitude were not affected. After awrite operation, the wiggle pulse width and amplitude changed; but, the area under the extracted pulses remained constant. Shifts in the peaks of reproduced waveforms increased when wiggles were close to the peak of the reproduced waveform, and the wiggle amplitude increased.

articleTitle: Three Dimensional Analytical Head Field Model of a Perpendicular Recording Head
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: We previously described a simple, analytical three-dimensional head field model of a perpendicular recording head with a soft magnetic underlayer. In that model, we assumed the presence of two magnetically charged planes to obtain the head field at the region close to the head, surface and under the pole tip. For simplicity of calculation, the charge distribution was approximated by a step function. However, it was found that the field can be obtained analytically from a charge distribution given by a+1/(b-cx<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) more accurately than from a step function approximation. In this paper, the derivation of the modified method is explained, and head fields obtained by the modified model are compared with those of the previous model and with large-scale experimental results. The modified model gives smoother head fields and better agreement with large-scale experimental results than the previous model.

articleTitle: Study on Secondary Gap in Sendust MIG Heads
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Sendust MIG heads were constructed with an oxide or noble metal layer deposited at the interface between the Sendust film and the ferrite. AES studies indicated that the deposition of barrier films such as Ir, Pt and SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> prevents the thermal diffusion of oxygen and hence oxidation of the Sendust film at the interface. The intensities of the (110) X-ray diffraction peak from initial Sendust layers deposited on a barrier film over MnZn ferrite were larger than for Sendust layers deposited directly on the MnZn ferrite. As a consequence, a MIG head constructed with Ir or SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> film between the Sendust film and the MnZn ferrite had a greatly reduced secondary gap effect.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Perpendicular Magnetic Rigid Disk by Non-Flying Single-Pole Head
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The feasibility of contact perpendicular magnetic rigid disk recording was investigated using non-flying single-pole heads. Double-layered magnetic films for use in perpendicular recording were fabricated by RF sputtering onto non-textured glass substrates. A novel head supporting and sliding method was introduced to enable contact rigid disk recording. By this method, the head can be floated at an extremely small spacing of 20 to 30 nm over the disk, loaded only by its own weight of less than 1 g. Using a non-flying head slider, not only were high-density recording characteristics obtained, but the heads and disks were observed to be remarkably durable, as much so as heads and media used in contact recording and reproduction with flexible perpendicular magnetic disk media.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties and Large Barkhausen Effect of FeCo, FeCr, FeNi System Amorphous Wires
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Fe-rich and Co-rich amorphous magnetostrictive wires have shown sensitive bistable flux reversal (large Barkhausen effect or re-entrant flux reversal) characteristics. Fe-Co, Fe-Cr and Fe-Ni system amorphous wires were prepared, and their various magnetic properties (M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>, M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>/M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>, K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub>, θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>, H*, and θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>/K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub>) were measured to investigate the general properties of the large Barkhausen effect and stress sensitivity of such amorphous wire. A domain wall propagates through an inner core of diameter about 1/√2 times that of positive-magnetostriction wires, and about 1/√3 times that of negative-magnetostriction wires. The stress sensitivity of magnetization was analyzed using a figure of merit F defined as (3/2) θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> (1-(M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>/M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) (M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>/M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>)/K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub>.

articleTitle: Permalloy Electrodeposited Films with the Addition of Sn
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Magnetic nickel-iron alloy films with added Sn were plated in a citric bath (a bath containing sodium citrate and citric acid) employing a periodic current-pulse plating technique with synchronous agitation. Agitation was periodically applied during part of the cycle current-off time (approximately 15 sec) and stopped just before the cycle current-on time (1 sec). The precise Sn-, Fe-and Ni-content dependencies of H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>, μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</sub>, B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> and H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> of films were clarified for compositions centered on the bulk permalloy composition, and the hardness H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">v</sub> and etch rate were compared with those of some electroplated alloy films (81 Ni-Fe, 45 Ni-Fe, permalloy with added Sn). The addition of Sn to Ni-Fe electroplated films not only resulted in excellent soft magnetic properties, but also acted to improve the film chemical and mechanical properties.

articleTitle: A New Micro-Switching Regulator Using a Planar-Type Magnetic Core
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The operation of a new micro-switching regulator using a planar-type magnetic core is described. The planar-type micro-magnetic core consists of Co-Zr amorphous magnetic films and zigzag-pattern coils, and is used as the main transformer in the switching regulator. When the core is driven at the parallel resonance frequency of the inductance and the stray capacitance of the coil, highly efficient regulator operation is expected, because the core loss is reduced when using a constant-voltage power supply. At a driving frequency of 1 MHz, the output and efficiency are 0.54 W and 30% respectively. Excellent voltage regulation is also achieved over a wide load-current range.

articleTitle: Behavior of Soft Magnetic Backlayer in Recording and Reproducing Process on Perpendicular Magnetic Recording Media
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Double layered Co-Cr perpendicular recording media were studied with respect to effect of a Ti thin intermediate layer between the Co-Cr and Ni-Fe layers on recording and reproducing characteristics. The increase of the output voltage by introduction of the Ti layer was explained by the increase of the effective permeability of the total system of the perpendicular head and back layer of the D.L. medium. It was found that the highly permeable back layer achieved by using the Ti layer induces a broadened waveform and an increase of peakshift of reproduced pulses. We concluded that media without a Ti layer are superior to those with a Ti layer with respect to the recording resolution.

articleTitle: Distance Sensors Utilizing Large Barkhausen Effect of Amorphous Wires
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: New distance sensors are described which utilize the large Barkhausen effect of amorphous magnetostrictive wires.
