Only one domain wall propagates in the direction of the wire axis under a driving magnetic field H when the condition H* ≫ H ≫ H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is satisfied throughout the length of the wire, where H* is the critical field for nucleation of reverse domains, and H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is the critical field for domain wall displacement. A distance sensor with a nonlinearity of less than 0.7% full-scale throughout a length of 1000 mm was fabricated using a cold-drawn and then heat-treated Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">77.5</sub>Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7.5</sub>B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</sub> amorphous wire of diameter 30 μm and length 1400 mm, in which the wall velocity v<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">w</sub> = 2M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>(H-H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>)/ß is controlled by increasing H*.

articleTitle: Magnetic properties of Fe based compositionally modulated nitride alloy films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: In the Co-metal based compositionally modulated nitride alloy films, we have noted the fact that the affinity in regards to nitrogen differs among metal elements such as Co and Nb. We have examined systems which contain the metallic elements (Nb) and metalloid elements (B) which have a strong affinity towards nitrogen as Fe-based compositionally modulated nitride alloy films. Based on this, the compositionally modulated nitride alloy films in the Fe-Nb alloys and the Fe-Nb-Si-B alloys show high saturation magnetization and good soft magnetic properties after high temperature annealing. Thus, their suitability as soft magnetic alloy films for use with magnetic heads has become clear. Herein, we report on Fe-based compositionally modulated nitride alloy films. Using the reactive sputtering method, Fe-based compositionally modulated nitride alloy film (CMNF) was formed.

articleTitle: Effects of Anisotropy Field Vector Distribution in a Recording Medium on Recording Characteristics--FEM Simulation with 3-D Magnetization Model
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A three-dimensional model of medium magnetization was developed to analyze the recording performance of particulate coated media. Using an FEM program incorporating this model, we investigated the process of recording by a ring head with respect to the effects of changes in the distributions of the easy-axis direction and of the anisotropy field strength, that is, the distributions of the orientation, size and shape of particles. It was shown that a sharper anisotropy field distribution gives a larger remanent magnetization in the medium at higher recording densities, but a sharper easy-axis distribution does not improve the high-density recording characteristics, because an AC erasure-like effect becomes dominant, owing to the broad perpendicular field component of ring heads.

articleTitle: Preparation of Mn2Sb:X (X = Bi,Cr) Films and Their Magnetic and Magnetooptical Properties
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Mn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Sb films prepared by vacuum evaporation are known to be perpendicular magnetization films. The effect on the magnetic and magnetooptical properties of Mn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Sb films of adding Bi and Cr was investigated over a wide range of compositions, extending up to 26 at% Bi and 16.4 at% Cr. Samples remained perpendicular magnetization films even when such large amounts of the third element were added, but the substitution of Bi for Sb is estimated from magnetic and AES measurements to be only about 8 at%, with the remaining Bi precipitated at the free surface of the film. The magnetooptical Faraday rotation angle at λ = 633 nm was decreased as a third element was added. Since Bi-and Cr-modified Mn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Sb intermetallic compounds are known to undergo a first-order phase transition from antiferromagnetic to ferrimagnetic behavior, these films (films containing Cr in particular) may find applications in temperature sensors which make use of the phase transition temperature.

articleTitle: An Analysis of Orthogonal-Core Type Push-Pull Parametric Transformer with Nonlinear Load
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The authors report an analysis of the orthogonal-core type push-pull parametric transformer with nonlinear load. The oscillation voltage and input current of the parametric transformer are calculated when a bidirectional triode-thyristor is connected to the output of the transformer on the basis of the magnetic circuit model of the orthogonal-core. The analytical results show good agreement with the experimental ones, and the push-pull parametric transformer has almost sinusoidal input current and high input power factor when the transformer has a nonlinear load such as a bidirectional triode-thyristor.

articleTitle: Metal Particulate Medium for Ultra High Density Recording
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Metal particulate (MP) test tape was prepared with playback characteristics nearly as good as those of ME tape, using very fine metal particles (average length 0.175&3x003BC;m) with average axial ratio 9, employing techniques for high dispersion and longitudinal orientation. In essence, these techniques are conventional; however, the test tape boasts superior characteristics making it suitable for use in ultra-high density recording, including a surface roughness of 3.63 nm (R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rms</sub>) and a squareness ratio of 0.89. Playback characteristics are also superior: the output level is only 1.5 dB lower than for ME tape at 100 kFRPI. In this paper, we describe the recording density characteristics of this test tape, and demonstrate the effect of an improved squareness ratio and surface roughness on the high-density characteristics, as well as the effect of employing heads with different B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> on the latter characteristics.

articleTitle: Effects of dielectric layers on TbFeCo magneto-optical disk
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: In the present work, we examine the possibilities for enhancing the sensitivity and reliability of magneto-optical disks, mainly from the standpoint of the refractive index and thermal properties of various kinds of dielectric films.

articleTitle: Analysis of Linear Parametric Motor Based on a New Magnetic Circuit Model
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: This paper describes an analysis of the behavior of a linear parametric motor. The primary of the linear motor uses a 4-legged laminated iron core and the secondary is constructed with aluminum plate and Fe-Si sheets. The oscillation voltage, currents and static thrust of the linear motor are calculated numerically based on a magnetic circuit model. The calculated values agree well with the measured ones. The analytical method presented here is useful for the optimum design of a linear parametric motor with 4-legged core.

articleTitle: The write phase characteristics in thick magnetic recording media
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Since the shape of recording magnetic fields remains as an isophase magnetic surface in the recording media with a relatively thick magnetic film such as magnetic tape, a notable write phase shift in the recording and playback system appears. Therefore, influences such as changes in the recording spacing are a matter of conern. Consequently, in order to carry out suitable equalization, the write phase characteristics in' the recording and playback system are monitored and the equalization circuit must compensate for them. Based on the above observations, we have measured the write phase characteristics of the recording and playback system and examined the influence of the recording system parameters and also studied the influence on the playback waveform.

articleTitle: Substrate Temperature Effect on Magnetic Properties and Microstructure of Vacuum Deposited Co-Cr Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The authors investigated the effect of substrate temperature and substrate thickness on the magnetic properties and microstructure of vacuum-deposited Co-Cr films. The microstructure of films is sufficiently dependent on the substrate temperature that the columnar structure disappears as the temperature rises from 250°C to 290°C, causing deterioration of the film recording characteristics. The substrate thickness dependence of the film magnetic properties is small; this result is consistent with simulations of the thickness dependence of the substrate temperature during deposition.

articleTitle: Recording and Reproducing Efficiency of Main-Pole Driven Perpendicular Magnetic Head
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The reproducing efficiency of a perpendicular magnetic recording head was investigated. Miniaturization and adoption of a head construction with a closed magnetic circuit and coil wound close to the main pole are very effective ways to improve the readout efficiency. We have designed and fabricated a main pole-driven perpendicular head with a thin film coil wound around the main pole film in addition to the wire coil. The readout voltage per turn of the thin film coil was confirmed to be double that of the wire coil, and the same readout voltage as from a thin film perpendicular head with a double-sided return path core can be obtained when the two coils of this head are used in series.

articleTitle: A Study of Improvement of Characteristics of Cloth Transformer Based on Equivalent Circuit Analysis
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: "Cloth" or woven-pattern transformers are very thin, and are anticipated to be useful in the MHz frequency region. We calculated the characteristics of cloth transformers using an equivalent circuit and taking account of stray capacitances. In order to improve the instrument's characteristics, the exciting reactance must be increased. The inductance per unit volume at a given driving frequency was calculated on the basis of simple assumptions. Analysis indicated that there exists a suitable ratio of the diameters of amorphous wire and copper wire.

articleTitle: Side Crosstalk Response in Perpendicular Magnetic Recording with Narrow Track Width Single-pole Head
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: We investigated the off-track side crosstalk response and Bitter patterns in perpendicular magnetic recording media after recording with a single-pole head, for various head track widths and recorded bit lengths. A Co-Cr/permalloy flexible 3.5" disk medium and single-sided single-pole heads with track widths of 3.8, 5.5 and 7.0 μm were used in evaluations. Experiments yielded the following results: 1) the recorded track width coincided precisely with the width of the main pole, even at the very narrow track width of 3.8 μm; 2) side crosstalk in perpendicular magnetic recording is governed by the side-reading behavior of the single-pole head used.

articleTitle: A Study on Recorded Transitions in Particulate Perpendicular Recording Media
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The shapes of recorded transitions in a perpendicular recording medium were studied experimentally, using a large-scale model consisting of a single-pole head and a particulate recording layer with an underlayer. Magnetization distributions were obtained from the measured magnetic field distributions at the medium surface. The results show that the shapes of the transitions strongly depend on the write current values and the initial erasifig conditions. The optimum write current for the large-scale medium corresponds to the value that generates a field 2.6 times larger than the coercivity at the center of the medium.

articleTitle: Large Barkhausen Effect of 6.3% SiFe Single Crystal Wire
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: New single-crystal 6.3% SiFe wires with diameters of less than 90 μm and lengths of from 7 to 30 cm were produced by the R&D Division of Toyobo Ltd. Sensitive and complete bistable flux reversal (the large Barkhausen effect or re-entrant flux reversal), similar to that seen in amorphous magnetostrictive wires, was found to occur in these wire samples. Single-crystal 6.3% SiFe wire exhibits almost zero magnetostriction. The mechanism of domain wall propagation along the wire axis is analyzed. Pulse generation characteristics measured for various magnetic fields and stresses are described.

articleTitle: Magnetic High-Frequency Inverters Using the Coupling of Two Non-Linear Oscillations
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The operation of self-oscillating type magnetic high-frequency inverters is described. These inverters utilize the coupling of two nonlinear oscillations which are generated in an orthogonal-flux type amorphous magnetic core, and consist of a Royer or Jensen circuit as an oscillator and the parametric oscillation circuit as an output transformer. The output of the inverters was 18 W at the high output frequency of 25 kHz, and excellent output voltage regulation, overload protection and noise filtering were obtained.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Co/Pr Artificial Superlattice Thin Films Evaporated in O2 Atmosphere
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Co/Pr artificial superlattice films were prepared by electron beam evaporation in O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> gas. The authors performed systematic investigations of the film magnetic properties, in particular (i) the dependence of the saturation magnetization M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> on temperature; (ii) the dependence of the perpendicular magnetic anisotropy constant K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⊥</sub> on temperature; and (iii) the dependence of the polar Kerr rotation angle θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> on wavelength. All the hysteresis loops of Co/Pr artificial superlattice films prepared in O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> gas were symmetric at 300 K, but a loop shift was observed for Co/Pr artificial superlattice films prepared in O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> gas at 1 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> Torr when films were cooled to 77 K in the presence of a magnetic field. The maximum loop shift was about 1.4 kOe. The dependence of θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> on wavelength for Co/Pr deposited in O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> gas is different from that for Co. Polar Kerr rotations were large, and the maximum value of θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> was - 0.77°.

articleTitle: Recording Characteristics on Pulse Train Write Current Waveform
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A magnetic recording head using separate read and write elements can have a reduced number of write coil turns. This facilitates write element fabrication for this kind of thin film head. However, a large current is required, and more heat is generated, when a square-wave write current waveform is used with fewer coil turns. A pulse train write current waveform represents one solution to this problem, by reducing heat generation, cross feed and power dissipation. We discuss the possibility of high-density magnetic recording using pulse train recording. A write head with a two-turn coil and an MR read head were used in experiments. We found no significant difference in the write head characteristics over the characteristics for a conventional square-wave NRZI write current waveform. Double-density NRZI pulse train recording best minimized the bit error rate, and a recording density more than double that for NRZI recording was attained.

articleTitle: Analysis of Head to Medium Magnetic Interaction in Perpendicular Magnetic Recording by Finite Element Method Combined with Magnetization Model
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A new simulation program has been developed for the analysis of perpendicular magnetic recording. This is the finite element method program which adopts a magnetization curling mode and a statistical method to calculate vectorial magnetizations in a medium. Using this simulation analysis, we could explain quantitatively the effects of the magnetic interaction between a single-pole head and a double-layer medium which were predicted from the experimental results. Furthermore, we were able to analyze a vectorial recording and reproducing mechanism. This new program is a very powerful tool which can more precisely simulate the magnetic recording process.

articleTitle: Fabrication of a Composite Inductance Using Co-Metal Amorphous Multilayer Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Multilayer films consisting of Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">84</sub>Zr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5.5</sub>Nb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10.5</sub> and Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">79</sub>Zr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub>Mo<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sub>Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> amorphous layers with SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> intermediate layers were prepared. An inductor for use in high frequency applications was fabricated from the film samples and an Ni-Zn ferrite yoke. In order to improve the high frequency characteristics, films fabricated into stripes were studied. Films were annealed in a magnetic field and the frequency response of multilayer films was measured at frequencies from 0.01 MHz to 200 MHz. Films with stripes showed better frequency characteristics than did films without stripes. An inductor fabricated from films with stripes with a total thickness of 20 μm and ferrite yokes exhibited an inductance of over 10 μH at 1 MHz, with frequency characteristics improved over those of Ni-Zn alone.

articleTitle: Magnetic Anisotropy of Ni Films Prepared by Ion Beam Sputtering
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetic anisotropy in Ni films deposited by ion beam sputtering (IBS), triode rf sputtering and diode rf sputtering, was studied in relation to the internal stress in the films. A strong in-plane easy-axis magnetic anisotropy (K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub> ≅ -5 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> erg/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>) was observed in IBS Ni films deposited at room temperature under an accelerating voltage exceeding 1 kV. The internal compressive stress was found to be as large as -1.2 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup> dyn/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, which caused a stress-induced magnetic anisotropy of about -1.2 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> erg/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> in the IBS Ni films. There is some positive contribution to the magnetic anisotropy, possibly due to the anisotropic internal shape effect (K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">int</sub> ≅ = 6 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> erg/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>). Both this perpendicular magnetic anisotropy and the stress-induced in-plane anisotropy decreased with increasing substrate temperature during deposition. It is possible to obtain a stress-free, isotropic IBS Ni film at an appropriate substrate temperature (250 to 300°C) and at an appropriate ion beam accelerating voltage (1.1 kV).

articleTitle: Structures and Saturation Magnetic Flux Density of Epitaxially Grown Fe and Fe-N Films on GaAs (100)
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Fe and Fe-N films were deposited on GaAs (100) substrates using an MBE system. 100 Å thick Fe single-crystal films were grown at substrate temperatures between 300°C and 400°C, at a rate of 1 Å/sec. Fe-N films of thickness 1000 Å were then grown at a rate of 0.04 Å/sec. The α" (Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) Phase was grown epitaxially on Fe single-crystal film at 100°C. The relationship among the crystal orientations of the α" (Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>), α-Fe and GaAs was (001)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Fel6N2//</sub>(110)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Fe</sub> //(110)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GaAs</sub> and [110]<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Fei6N2</sub> //[001]<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Fe</sub>//[001]<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GaAs</sub>. The saturation magnetic flux density (B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>) of this film was found to be 2.20 T, lower than the expected value of 2.83 T, although this value was 10% higher than for Fe single-crystal films on GaAs (100).

articleTitle: Recording Characteristics of Electroless-plated CoNiReP/NiWP Double Layers
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Electroless-plated CoNiReP/NiWP double layer films were investigated for perpendicular magnetic recording media as flexible disks. The magnetic properties of a CoNiReP recording layer, such as a saturation magnetization (M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">S</sub>) value and squareness ratio of perpendicular hysteresis loops (SQR (⊥)), were changed by NiWP underlayers. The reproduced output voltage of CoNiReP/NiWP flexible disks at low recording density with a ring-type head increased with M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">S</sub> values of recording layer and underlayer. Moreover, the D<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</sub> value of 172 kFRPI was attained by the highest SQR(⊥) medium of the double layer evaluated with a 0.20μm gap length sendust ring-type head. This may be mainly due to large perpendicular anisotropy of the top region of recording layer which is improved by the underlayer addition.

articleTitle: Structure and Magnetic Anisotropy of Fe-N Films Prepared by Ion Assisted Vapor Deposition
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Changes in the structure and magnetic properties of Fe-N films prepared by ion-assisted vapor deposition were examined, varying the ion current density and substrate temperature. The film structure was characterized by X-ray diffraction techniques and the magnetic anisotropy was evaluated by torque curve measurements. When both the ion current density and the substrate temperature are low, a uniaxial anisotropy is induced by ion bombardment. The origin of the uniaxial anisotropy is not known. With increasing ion current density and substrate temperature, a cubic film texture develops, and an anisotropy with four-fold symmetry appears. As the directions of closest-packed atoms in the film microstructure are coincident with the direction of ion incidence, it is thought that the dependence of the sputtering yield on the grain orientation causes the texture development. The results of experiments using other ion species (Ar, Ne) are also indicated.

articleTitle: Co-Cr Thin Films Deposited on Substrates with Island Structure
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effect of substrate morphology on the perpendicular anisotropy of Co-Cr films was studied. Co-Cr layers were deposited on top of Al-3 wt% Cu underlayers; the latter were of thickness 1.5 to 40 nm and were deposited at a substrate temperature of from 25 to 300°C. SEM photographs revealed an island structure for the Al-Cu films deposited at 300°C, while those deposited at 25°C had a flat surface. The Δ θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</sub> and H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">keff</sub> of Co-Cr films on Al-Cu underlayers deposited at 300°C were about 15° and 2 kOe respectively, while the figures when the Al-Cu layer was deposited at 25°C were under 10° and about 3 kOe respectively. The morphology of the Al-Cu underlayer thus greatly influenced the perpendicular anisotropy of the Co-Cr film.

articleTitle: Amorphous Fiber Core Head with Low Power Dissipation for Magnetic Field Modulation on Magneto-Optic Recording
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: CoFeSiB system soft magnetic amorphous fiber with an as-drawn diameter of about 10 μm (AMFD) exhibits a unique B-H loop in the MHz range. We determined that if the AMFD core is used at about 1 kG at 1 MHz, the core loss is extremely low (1.7 J/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>), although the permeability is also low (200). We designed and fabricated a magnetic head employing an AFMD core for magneto-optical recording by magnetic field modulation, with an AMFD bundle center core piece 1 mm in diameter. Comparison of the AMFD core head with a conventional ferrite head shows that losses in the former are about 60% of those in the latter, under the same conditions of magnetic field and inductance.

articleTitle: Relationship between Deviations of Dipole Orientation and Position in MEG Topography
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: This study focuses on the influence of inhomogeneities in the human head on surface magnetic fields generated by radial dipoles inside the head. Using a simple inhomogeneous spherical model, components of magnetic fields perpendicular to the surface of the sphere are calculated, and the spatial distributions of MEGs are simulated. The influences of both rotation or inclination of the dipole orientation and shifting of the dipole position on the spatial distributions of MEGs were investigated. It is shown that when the dipole orientation is inclined from the radial direction, the spatial patterns of MEGs are analogous to the results when the dipole position is shifted. The effect of inhomogeneities of brain lesions on the spatial MEG patterns produced by radial dipoles is also studied.

articleTitle: Preparation of Substituted Ba-Ferrite Small Particles by Hydrothermal Synthetic Method Accompanied by Heat Treatment and Their Magnetic Properties
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Fine Co-Ti substituted barium ferrite particles (500 to 1000 Å) with high dispersibility and highly uniform size were fabricated by a hydrothermal synthetic method accompanied by heat treatment, and their magnetic properties were studied. Sample characterization relied on X-ray diffraction, Mössbauer spectra obtained with a 16.4 kOe field applied parallel to the incident γ-rays showed the formation of a plane of easy magnetization in Co-Ti substituted barium ferrite, which may be the origin of an abrupt magnetic softening of this system even at low substitution levels. An increased saturation magnetization was obtained by lowering the Ti content from the equimolecular ratio with Co ions.

articleTitle: Shape of Magnetization Curves
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The shape of magnetoresistivity curves is discussed with reference to the rotation model of magnetization. The magnetoresistivity curve exhibits a dip when the magnetic field deviates from the direction of hard magnetization. Deviation of the direction of electric current from the easy axis direction causes an irreversibility in the magnetoresistivity curve. These results indicate that the fact that the dip and/or irreversibility is independent of the Barkhausen effect should be taken into account in explanations of experimentally observed curves. An asymmetric magnetoresistivity curve sometimes observed for 82Ni-Fe permalloy films is explained by the model, with the assumption of magnetic inhomogeneity. The shape of magnetoresistivity curves observed for Co/Au multilayer films with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy is also explained by the model.

articleTitle: Effects of NiFe Underlayer on the Properties of CoCr Layer in Perpendicular Double-Layered Media
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: CoCr/NiFe double-layered perpendicular media were sputter-deposited onto NiP-plated aluminum substrates. The crystal orientation and magnetic properties of the CoCr layer on NiFe are poorer than those of CoCr on Nip. In order to improve the properties of CoCr/NiFe film, the effects of the NiFe underlayer were investigated with respect to the surface roughness, crystal orientation and crystallinity. It was found that the crystallinity of the NiFe layer strongly affects the crystal orientation of the CoCr layer. Both bias sputtering and a low residual gas pressure were effective for improving the NiFe crystallinity. The c-axis dispersion angle (Δ θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</sub>) was as small as 1.6° for CoCr on a highly crystalline NiFe layer.

articleTitle: Development of 18 Track 2 Layer Thin Film Head Using All Dry Process
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: An eighteen-track, two-layer thin film write head, fabricated using only dry processes, has been developed for use in magnetic tape drive systems. The all-dry production relies on repeated sputtering and ion milling processes. In smoothing processes, two kinds of resist were used, and the maximum step size was 200 Å. The front taper angle could be controlled between 30 and 45°. The head employed a Co-Nb-Zr-Ta amorphous alloy with high B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> (12,000 G), developed to enable complete writing of the medium. The Co-Nb-Zr-Ta amorphous film was deposited by bias sputtering. The AYA-2L (for Active Yoke by Amorphous-2 Layer) head was developed as an enhanced write head fabricated using only dry processes.

articleTitle: Characteristics of Soft Heating Method Using Temperature Sensitive Amorphous Flakes
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The soft heating method is a means of induction heating utilizing temperature-sensitive magnetic materials implanted within human tissue. In this method, the Curie temperature acts as a reference temperature. In this paper we propose a soft heating element made of temperature-sensitive amorphous flakes in order to heat deepseated tumors effectively. We also discuss the heating characteristics of a mixture of amorphous flakes and ferrite powders.

articleTitle: A 3.5-inch 16MB floppy disk drive
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Along with the spread of OA equipment such as personal computers, work stations and word processors, the flexible magnetic disk drive (FDD) is increasing in importance as an external memory device which can be moved among different equipment. In addition, FDDs are in demand in various applications and areas such as OS software delivery, HDD back-up and software which contains video and voice data. There is, however, a need for improvement of memory capacity, boosting of the data transfer rate and miniaturization. In line with these targets, we would like to report on the development of a 3.5 inch 16 MB flexible magnetic disk drive. In particular, we will focus on an explanation of the drive itself, the processing of the recording and reproduction signal and the host interface.

articleTitle: Development of MFM-SEM System for Observation of Magnetic Domains
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetic force microscope (MFM) has the potential of enabling observations of fine magnetic domain structures, but remaining problems must be resolved before practical application is possible. As a result of theoretical analysis, the most suitable values of the probe-sample distance h and probe radius R were found to be h = 600 Å and R = 100 Å. Using these values, an MFM cantilever of length 130 μm, width 10 μm and thickness 1 μm was designed. A scanning tunneling microscope (STM) was used to detect the cantilever displacement resulting from the magnetic force. A new domain configuration was observed by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) by bringing a sharp Fe wire tip close to a sample and observing the influence of the leakage field of the tip.

articleTitle: A Study on Magnetic Properties of Fe4N Powders
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Magnetization and Mössbauer spectra were measured for three kinds of Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>N powders made from acicular α-FeOOH, α-Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> and carbonyl iron powders. Except for the Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>N powder from carbonyl iron, the saturation magnetization was lower than the bulk value (190 emu/g). A large amount of oxygen and small amounts of Ni, Zn and Si were detected in the sample obtained from α-FeOOH. From the Mössbauer spectra, it was concluded that decreases in the saturation magnetization were mainly due to the coexistence of a paramagnetic phase. A large quadrupole splitting of the paramagnetic peak indicates that the paramagnetic phase may be an oxide consisting of Fe(II) ions, e.g. wustite. In addition, it is thought that Ni and Zn preferentially substitute for Fe at the corner sites of fcc Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>N, and also reduce the magnetization.

articleTitle: Recording Characteristics and Durability of Fe-Co-O/Fe-Co Double-Layered Perpendicular Magnetic Recording Medium
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: In order to enhance the perpendicular magnetic recording characteristics of an Fe-Co-O medium with a large perpendicular anisotropy, an Fe-Co underlayer with a coercive force of about 100 Oe was investigated. The voltage reproduced from the Fe-Co-O/Fe-Co double-layered medium with the most suitable film thickness is five times as large as that for a single-layered medium. However, an Fe-Co-O/Ni-Fe double-layered medium, the underlayer of which has a higher permeability, did not show such great improvement in reproduced voltage. These results suggest that the effect of the Fe-Co underlayer is different from the decrease of demagnetization field caused by the Ni-Fe layer in a Co-Cr/Ni-Fe double-layered medium. It was also verified that Fe-Co-O/Fe-Co double-layered flexible disks have a high wear resistance, with a lifetime of more than 10 million passes without a protection layer, because of the higher stiffness and stronger adhesive force between the Fe-Co layer and the polyimide substrate.

articleTitle: Effect of Side-Fringing Field on Read-Write Characteristics for Thin Film Magnetic Heads
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The side-fringing fields of thin film heads were studied using three-dimensional simulations. Playback signals were calculated using the reciprocity principle. The output as a function of linear density was calculated by superpositioning of isolated pulses. The results of three-dimensional calculations of isolated pulses, off-tracking and output as a function of linear density, agreed with measurements. These calculations and measurements indicated that the effect of the side-fringing field appears in the isolated pulses from narrow-track heads. It was found that asymmetry in isolated pulses results from the effect of the side-fringing field. By narrowing the track width, the effect of the side-fringing field is increased. Playback pulses from the outside of the track are broader than those at the track center, and so the resolution of narrow-track heads decreases.

articleTitle: Analysis of Ferroresonant Voltage Stabilizer with Filter
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The performance of a ferroresonant voltage stabilizer with a filter connected is described. In carrying out the analysis, a phasor method was adopted for the linear circuit, and a discrete Fourier transform was used for the nonlinear circuit. From the results obtained by numerical analysis, the optimum circuit constants, which stabilize the output voltage and minimize the self-capacitance of the equipment, were derived. Also, it was found that the input current and output voltage waveform can be improved under these conditions. The analysis results were confirmed by experiments.

articleTitle: Feasibility study of a high capacity 2-inch-data-disk-system
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Basic studies were performed on the head/medium interface and transducing system of projected high-capacity 2" data disk systems with a formatted storage capacity of 1.44 MB (equal to that of 2HD 3.5" mini-floppy disk drives), and with roughly double the unformatted capacity of existing 2" data disk systems, with the following conclusions: (1) Upon comparing fixed-pad, moving-pad and negative-pressure-plate interfaces, it was found that a negative-pressure-plate assembly is best suited for use over an expanded disk area. (2) Through use of the negative-pressure-plate method, it was possible to increase the number of tracks to 90 using a single side of the disk, with the same track pitch (100 pm) as in current systems. (3) By optimizing the transducing system (gap depth and number of coil windings) in accordance with a minimum recording wavelength of 0.69 pm, it was found that pre-erase type ferrite heads could provide adequate performance. (4) In using an enlarged portion of the disk, it becomes necessary to switch between different equalization characteristics at a disk radial position nearly midway between the innermost and outermost tracks. This switching can be accomplished simply by changing the parameters of the equalization circuit used in existing systems. (5) Drawing on the above results, we developed a prototype high-capacity 2" data disk system which preserves compatibility with systems currently in use. The prototype was found to provide performance (error rates, environmental conditions, durability) comparable to that of current systems.

articleTitle: Effect of Yoke Pattern on Recording Characteristics of Thin Film Heads
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The authors studied the dependence of the magnetic anisotropy of thin film heads on the core side angle. Because of the increase in core reluctance, it had been thought that the head efficiency decreases with increasing side angle. However, measurements revealed that the head efficiency increases with the side angle. To determine the reason for the unexpected behavior, three-dimensional calculations of the stress and stress-induced anisotropy were performed. According to these analyses, the magnitude of the tensile stress along the hard axis increases with the side angle, and therefore the anisotropy field is lower when the magnetic layer of the head has a positive magnetostriction constant. A decrease in the anisotropy field was confirmed by observations using the magneto-optical Kerr effect. It was concluded that the side angle affects the magnitude of the magnetic anisotropy, in addition to the core reluctance and the domain structure.

articleTitle: Feasibility of Multi-Track Perpendicular Magnetic Recording
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Basic studies were performed to investigate the feasibility of multitrack recording. It was confirmed that the side-writing and side-erasing effects of a single-pole type perpendicular magnetic head are negligibly small. It was also found that the perpendicular head possesses uniform reproduce sensitivity in the track width direction of the main pole. These results show that perpendicular recording is suitable for multitrack recording and full-track reproduction using multilevel recording.

articleTitle: Compensation Method for Phase Distortion of Output Voltage in the Three-phase Triport UPS System
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A new three-phase constant-voltage transformer is described. In this circuit, load unbalance and input voltage asymmetry can in principle be removed by ring-connected compensation windings. When the, triac of an Automatic Voltage Regulator (AVR) is controlled to give a constant output voltage, phase differences between the output voltages are kept at 120°. This principle can also be applied to conventional three-phase constant-voltage transformers with magnetic shunts and to three-phase Triport UPS systems.

articleTitle: Finite element analysis of metal-in-gap head write-fields
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The authors employ the two-dimensional (2D) non-linear finite element analysis to analyze the write field, in order to optimize the design of metal-in-gap (MIG) heads. They clarify the contribution of the MIG head to increases in the linear recording density, focusing on not only the strength but also the gradient of the write field. Finally, they describe the trial fabrication of heads reflecting the analysis results, and show that the read/write characteristics expected on the basis of the write field analysis were actually obtained.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Cast and Hot-Pressed Pr-Fe-B Magnets
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A new process has been developed to produce high-energy-product bulk Pr-Fe-B magnets without the handling of any magnetic powder or powder-like ribbons. This process consists of three main steps, casting, hot-pressing and annealing, and it minimizes the oxygen contamination of magnets. A typical composition of a cast alloy is Pr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">76.5</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.5</inf>. Using this type of alloy, crystal alignment along the c-axis is easily induced by hot-pressing. Copper plays two important roles in this process: its addition simultaneously achieves high coercivity and excellent magnetic alignment. The magnetic properties of hot-pressed Pr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">76.5</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.5</inf> magnets are: B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> = 12.5 kG, iH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> = 10.0 kOe, and (BH)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> = 36.2 MGOe. The cast alloy of this composition also has an iHc of 7.3 kOe and a (BH)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> of 9.2 MGOe after annealing at 1000°C for 24 hours. The step rise in the initial magentization curve indicates a nucleation-controlled coercivity mechanism.

articleTitle: Novel Magneto-Optical Media with Direct Overwritability by Exchange-Coupled Quadrilayer Film
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A direct overwrite method by light intensity modulation using only an external magnet is described. The recording medium consists of an exchange-coupled RE-TM alloy quadrilayer film. Good recording characteristics were obtained, including a C/N ratio of better than 47 dB at a bit length of 0.76 μm without a residual signal. The process in which the second layer is initialized is particularly important. M-H loop measurements revealed that the second layer has two different coercivities with respect to the magnetization states of the other layers; the coercivity of the second layer is smaller than that of a single layer of the same material when the sublattice magnetization of the first layer is antiparallel to the fourth layer magnetization. These phenomena aid in the initialization of the second layer.

articleTitle: Relation between the Exciting Voltage Waveform and the Stability of Oscillation in the Parametric Motor
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The relation between the exciting voltage waveforms and the stability of oscillation in the parametric motor is discussed. The main conclusions drawn from this study are as follows: (1) The stable region of the parametric motor excited by square wave voltage is larger than that excited by triangular and sinusoidal wave voltage. (2) The parameter which has a direct effect upon the stability of parametric oscillation is the time variation of inductance.

articleTitle: Soft Magnetic Properties of Fe-Ni-Nb Alloy Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The relation between the soft magnetic properties and local anisotropy fluctuation measured by the dynamic differential susceptibility method in Fe-Ni-Nb alloy films was clarified and discussed in comparison with Fe-Si-Al alloy films. Fe-Ni-Nb alloy films with excellent soft magnetic properties, 5 MHz values of μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</sub> = 6500 for 1000 Å thick films were obtained. For Fe-Si-Al alloy films, the magnitude of μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</sub> = 6500 is proportional to 1/S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (where S is a structure constant) and independent of the value of H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub>, while for Fe-Ni-Nb alloy films, the value of S is about one-tenth of that in Fe-Si-Al alloy films, and the magnitude of μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</sub> 6500 does not depend on S. Rather, this magnitude is dependent on the value of H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub>, and is almost equal to 4πM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>/H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub>, obtained from a rotational magnetization model in a uniaxial single-domain particle.

articleTitle: Study of a Trial Production of Magnetic Gear with Variable Circular Arc Tooth Profile
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The design and overlap area of permanent magnets in meshing area and performance characteristics of circular arc magnetic gear are described. The transmitted torque or circular arc magnetic gear increases by 6% as compared to an involute magnetic gear of the same dimensions. This phenomenon is a result of the increase in the permanent magnet overlap area increasing in the meshing area using a variable pinion arc tooth profile.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Magnetic Fluids near Melting Point
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetization (M), field-induced magnetic anisotropy (Ku), rotational hysteresis loss (E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rot</inf>) and melting point (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>) of water-and paraffin-base ferrofluids were investigated in the temperature range from 77 K~300°K, as functions of the density of the colloidal particles. Both paraffin and paraffin-base fluids were melted down at temperatures between 180 and 210°K. In this range, the values of M and E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rot</inf> for paraffin-base fluids increased, and the K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</inf> decreased, with increasing temperature. These properties may be explained by assuming that liquid-state and solid-state regions exist in the paraffin in this temperature range, and that the volume of the solid-state region decreased with increasing temperature. Depression of the freezing point was observed in water-base fluids.

articleTitle: Preparation of LIPS (Longitudinally oriented Inside and Perpendicularly oriented at Surface) Dual Oriented Tapes Using Co-γ-Fe2O3
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: In order to improve the dual layer structure of LIPS tapes, by improving the perpendicularity of the surface layer and the longitudinal orientation of the inside layer, infrared irradiation under a perpendicular holding field was added to the "surface air-dry" stage. A tape thus obtained showed a higher playback output at both short and long wavelengths than for previous tapes with an oblique orientation over their entire thickness. The dual-layer tape had a playback output higher by 5 dB than for longitudinal tape at λ = 0.7 μm. Particles with a small aspect ratio (approximately 5) proved to be suitable for use in perpendicular tapes because of their resistance to calendering disorientation. This effect was confirmed by SQRz measurements.

articleTitle: High Speed Magnetic Field Modulation in Pit-Edge Magneto-Optic Recording II
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: As one approach to high-speed high-density magneto-optical disk systems, we studied the application of pit-edge record ing by magnetic field modulation, in which data overwriting is possible. In overwriting, the erase behavior of the old data is crucial. Here, we trial-fabricated magneto-optical disks with the effective land width, which affects read/write performance, limited to about 0.8 μm, and confirmed that efficient erasure is possible. Moreover, on the basis of read/write characteristics, we clarified the relation between linear velocity and the magnetic field reversal frequency required for stable edge formation.

articleTitle: A Measurement of Ellipticity of Reflected Light for Magnetooptical Disk
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: It is possible to estimate the ellipticity of light reflected from a magnetooptical disk by determining the pickup phase difference which gives maximal readout signal amplitude. An optical pickup was fabricated with a phase compensator and half-wave plate; this pickup had a variable phase difference and enabled rotation of the plane of polarization of light incident on the disk. The two contributions to the ellipticity, substrate retardation and the Kerr ellipticity, were separated by measuring the ellipticity when the plane of polarization of the incident light was both parallel to and perpendicular to disk grooves. The result indicates that a polycarbonate disk contributes more to the ellipticity than does a glass disk. Also, it was verified that the temperature dependence of the ellipticity originates in variation of the substrate retardation.

articleTitle: A Method of Estimating Magnetic Reluctivity by Inverse Problems
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: We propose a method for estimating magnetic reluctivity for application in nondestructive testing and medical electronics. The combination of the finite element method and the measured data, one of the inverse problems, makes it possible to estimate magnetic reluctivity. Formulations for the estimation and the accuracy of the estimated values are reported. According to numerical experiments using these equations, we investigated the possibility of estimating the reluctivity of magnetic materials.

articleTitle: Ion-Assisted Effect on Ion-Beam Sputtered CoCr Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: CoCr films were prepared by dual ion beam sputtering on Ti-coated glass substrates. The film magnetic and crystallographic properties were investigated in relation to the ion-assisting conditions. Ion-assisted deposition with a low accelerating voltage of less than 200 V is very effective for increasing the perpendicular coercivity and decreasing the in-plane squareness; this fact implies that the initial film layer is thin. This method also promotes growth of a well-oriented columnar structure.

articleTitle: A Study of the Thinner Cr Underlayer in Co-Alloy/Cr for Rigid Disk
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: This work reports the effect of a thinner Cr underlayer in a longitudinal metal medium consisting of Co alloy on a Cr underlayer. Media with a thinner Cr underlayer exhibit improved signal-to-noise characteristics compared to media with a thicker Cr underlayer. This is a consequence of an increased saturation magnetic flux density B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> and squareness S, and decreased noise N. We think that the change in B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> is influenced by the level of diffusion between the Cr underlayer and the Co alloy film layer, that the change in S is affected by changes in the Co crystalline orientation, and that changes in N are due to changes in grain size.

articleTitle: Effect of Annealing Treatment on Magnetic Properties of Melt-Spun Nd-Fe-Co-B-V Ribbons
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Amorphous ribbons of Nd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">72</sub>Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sub>B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7.5</sub>V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.5</sub> alloy were prepared by the single-roller rapid-quenching method at a substrate surface velocity of 20.7 m/s, and the effect of annealing on the magnetic properties was studied. The optimum annealing conditions were 650°C for 5 min.; crystallized ribbon thus annealed had a (BH)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> of 148.6 kJ/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. TEM observations indicated that the fine grains of ribbons crystallized from the amorphous state were from 25 to 33 nm in diameter. The temperature coefficients (in the range 25 to 125°C) of B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> and H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cJ</sub> for ribbon crystallized from amorphous Nd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">72</sub>Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sub>B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7.5</sub>V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.5</sub> alloy were -0.083%/°C (reversible) and -0.375%/°C (irreversible), respectively. The maximum energy product obtained for a Nd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">72</sub>Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sub>B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7.5</sub>V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.5</sub> bonded magnet prepared from ribbons annealed at 650°C was 94.2 kJ/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>; under these conditions the bonded magnet had a density of 6.25 Mg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>.

articleTitle: Magnetoelastic Effects of Fe-Pd Base Alloys
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetoelastic properties of Fe-Pd+Mo,Ni,C and Si ternary alloys have been studied. The γ phase was stabilized at room temperature by the addition of the third element. The longitudinal magnetostriction λ″, ΔE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</sub> and dλ″/dH all increase on adding a third element. The magneto-mechanical coupling constant k obtained from the ΔE effect agrees with that calculated from the dynamic magnetostriction. The maximum value of k is 0.26 at a bias field of 8 Oe.

articleTitle: Soft Magnetic Properties of Multilayered Fe-2~4 at% Si Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Fe-3.4 at% Si/Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> multilayer films were prepared by rf sputtering. Soft magnetic properties were obtained when intermediate layers (SiN<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>) were deposited in an Ar+N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> atmosphere and had a composition ratio (N/Si) of about 4/3. articleTitle: Approximate Analysis of Perpendicular Magnetic Recording Characteristics
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: In perpendicular magnetic recording using a single pole type magnetic head and a double-layered medium, a sharp magnetization transition is formed in the Co-Cr layer of the medium because the demagnetizing field is minimized in the region of magnetization transition. Therefore, the shapes of isolated pulses can be easily calculated by a head field and a M-H loop of the medium. In this paper, a simple means of approximation for the analysis of an isolated pulse shape in perpendicular magnetic recording in described. For the analysis, the distribution of the head field is computed by FEM considering the head-to-medium magnetic interaction, and an actual M-H loop are used. The calculated narrow pulse width in perpendicular magnetic recording is compared with those measured and calculated in longitudinal magnetic recording.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties in Co/Ag and Fe/Ag Compositionally Modulated Multilayer Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magneto-optical and magnetic properties of Co/Ag and Fe/Ag compositionally modulated multilayer films (CMF's) were investigated. Co/Ag CMF's have better crystallinity and periodicity than Fe/Ag CMF's. An enhancement of θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> was also observed at the plasma edge of Ag metal in Co/Ag and Fe/Ag CMF's. The peak values of θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> in Co/Ag CMF's are larger than those in Fe/Ag CMF's. Moreover, the enhancement of θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> due to plasma resonance at the granularly crystallized grain boundary of Co and Ag was observed in heat-treated Co/Ag CMF's. A magnetic perpendicular anisotropy K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub> was induced in both CMF's when the modulation length D was decreased.

articleTitle: Xe Ion-Implanted NiFe Thin Films-Behaviors of Xenon and Magnetic Properties
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Systematic experiments were performed on xenon ion implantation into permalloy films, in order to understand the effects of implantation of heavy inert ions on microstructures and magnetic properties. Xenon ion implantation always caused crystallization of the partially epitaxially grown permalloy film, so that the grain size increased. In addition, spherical bubbles were clearly observed even at low ion fluence in slightly defocused TEM images. The bubble size varied over several tens of Angstroms with the fluence. In electron diffraction patterns, a weak extra ring became visible when the fluence exceeded about 6 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sup>/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Magnetization measurements showed a large decrease in Ms and Meff when the fluence increased. The origin of the decrease in magnetization is discussed in relation to xenon bubble formation; it is probably attributable to a decrease in the magnetization of permalloy alloy atoms on the bubble surface.

articleTitle: Temperature Dependence of Faraday Effect for Cd1-xMnxTe Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The Faraday effect in Cd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-xMn<sub>x</sub>Te films prepared by ionized-cluster beams has been analyzed theoretically. Faraday rotation spectra are calculated taking account of a broadening parameter Γ of exciton absorption in a nondegenerate second-order perturbation theory. The calculated spectra are compared with the experimental data of Cd<sub>1-x</sub>Mn<sub>x</sub>Te films. The results reveal that the thermal broadening of exciton absorption is due to the scattering of an exciton by longitudinal optical (LO) phonons.</inf>

articleTitle: Theoretical Study of the Characteristics of Modulation Noise in Magnetic Tapes
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: sinusoidal surface roughness were prepared, and modulation noise in the tapes was measured using a VHS format VCR. It was found that the modulation noise contained both amplitude-modulation (AM) and phase-modulation (PM) components; the AM and PM noise increased with increasing ratio of surface roughness to recording wavelength, and PM noise increased wih decreases in the ratio of thespatial wavelength of the tape surface roughness to the recording wavelength.

articleTitle: Changes in Magnetic Properties and Structure of Nitrogen Added Fe-Co Multilayered Films by Annealing
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Fe/Co multilayer films with nitrogen added were annealed in a vacuum with a 500 Oe rotating magnetic field. Annealing at an appropriate temperature causes decomposition of nitride phases such as Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>, Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> and (FeCo)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>N though the temperature at which such decomposition occurs increases from 200°C to 350°C as the layer period d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">layer</inf> is increased from 36 Å to 470 Å. The film accordingly loses its layered structure and becomes a uniform Fe-Co alloy film. Changes in the magnetization curve of films with the annealing temperature indicate that film with low coercivity is composed of Fe-N and Co-N layers with a small magnetic anisotropy and of Fe-Co-N layers with a large uniaxial magnetic anisotropy. Changes in the coercive force H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> with the annealing temperature depend on the compositional modulation wavelength d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">layer</inf>, though all films with d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">layer</inf> larger than 60 Å have nearly the same minimum H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> value of about 1 Oe.

articleTitle: Cotton-Mouton Spectrum in Cobalt-Substituted Magnetic Garnet
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Spectra of the Cotton-Mouton effect and Faraday rotation in cobalt-substituted magnetic garnet films were measured at wavelengths between 0.5 and 2.0 μm using a piezobirefringent modulator. Experimentally measured spectra were compared with those obtained by theoretical analysis within the framework of the ligand field theory. Satisfactory agreement between experiment and theory was obtained for a reasonable set of parameters.

articleTitle: Characteristics and Application of C-Shaped Magnetic Sheets
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The structure and characteristics of a new magnetic shielding device are described. This shielding device utilizes a certain magnetic circuit in which C-shaped magnetic sheets are combined in a cage-like shape. This is effective in both screening out the unwanted external field and in reducing the leakage flux from magnetic field generators. Because this device has space between magnetic sheets, it is useful for the cooling of magnetic field generators and allows a saving in the amount of magnetic material required.

articleTitle: Characteristics of a New Implantable Transformer with Planar Shape
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: This paper describes the output characteristics of a new transformer for an implantable artificial heart. The implantable transformer consists of Co-base amorphous magnetic fiber and conductive fibers. Features include a thin, planar shape and high flexibility. A trial-fabricated transformer can supply an electric power of 10 W. The magnetic field distribution in the vicinity of the transformer was measured, and it was possible to reduce the leakage flux behind it. A transformer with a spiral woven structure is also discussed.

articleTitle: A New Sputtering Target for Perpendicular Media Continuous Fabrication and Resultant Properties
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A new sputtering source target was proposed for use in high-rate deposition of double-layer perpendicular media. The target consisted of Permalloy plate walls which were perpendicular to the substrate and functioned as part of a magnetic circuit for plasma confinement. The discharge characteristics of the target were very well suited to low-pressure, high-power sputtering at a low discharge voltage. The Permalloy films obtained with this target had a broader region of uniform thickness and much stronger adhesion to polyimide substrate than did films prepared using a conventional GT target.

articleTitle: A Magneto-Optical Disk for Readout Using Circular Dichroism Effect
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A magneto-optical disk for readout based on the circular dichroism effect was investigated. Making use of this effect, the optical head construction can be simplified, because recorded bits are directly detected as the change in intensity of reflected light. We studied multilayer structure films as a means of enhancing the circular dichroism, and identified as promising a four-layer magneto-optical medium consisting of AlN, GdTbFe, AlN and Al. The readout signal quality was evaluated using an optical head, and a C/N ratio of 45 dB was achieved at a bit length of 1.3 μm.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties and Crystal Structures of Sputtered CoFe Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Sputtered Co-(15-19 at%) Fe films were prepared, varying the Ar gas pressure and substrate temperature as parameters. The relationships between the film magnetic properties and crystal structure were investigated. Films with an fcc phase (111) preferred orientation showed relatively high H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> values of more than 8 Oe and a B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> of about 19 kG. Films with a bec phase (110) preferred orientation showed low H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> values of 2 to 3 Oe, comparable to the values for single-layered Fe-base films, and a B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> of about 21 kG. It was verified that this difference in H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> is not attributable to differences in internal stress or in crystallite size.

articleTitle: Mock Test of Linear Pulse Motor-Driven Artificial Heart
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: This paper deals with the basic characteristics of a linear pulse motor-driven artificial heart, as obtained in mock tests. The artificial heart consists mainly of a linear pulse motor and a blood pump, which are mechanically coupled. The linear pulse motor has a flat structure, and is constructed from laminated sheets of permendure and rare-earth magnets. Two kinds of blood pumps, the diaphragm and the pusher-cup types, were prepared for use in mock tests. With the diaphragm-type pump, an aortic pressure of 69~103 mm Hg can be obtained at 113 bpm (beats/min). Using the pusher-cup type pump, an aortic pressure of 53~97 mm Hg was obtained at 130 bpm. The artificial heart was thus confirmed to have the potential for actual implantation.

articleTitle: Scattering Centers for Magnetoelastic Waves in Amorphous Wires
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Scattered magnetoelastic waves were observed in as-quenched and annealed amorphous Fe-Si-B wires in order to clarify the nature of the scattering centers. Neither a magnetic field nor tensile stress applied to the wire changed the waveform of the scattered waves. According to observations of scattered waves in annealed wire, the annealing process has no significant effect on the properties of the scattering centers. These experimental results indicate that the scattering centers are caused by fluctuations of some elastic properties along the wire which are introduced by the quenching process, and that they are spaced a few millimeters apart on average.

articleTitle: Magnetoresistance and Hall Effects for Fe-Ni-M Alloy Thin Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
